metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane has Stash Appeal Following Return
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) was activated off the Injured Reserve ahead of the Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. Lane has been sidelined since fracturing his wrist during the season opener. It's unclear what kind of role he's going to have during his first week back. Once he's back to full speed, Lane could find himself in a decent role as the WR2 of this offense. The rookie wideout looked great during camp, so we'll see what he can do now. Fantasy managers looking for help at the wide receiver spot should consider stashing Lane. He probably won't be a great option for this weekend, but he should be able to help fantasy managers down the road.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) activated off of IR, will play against Cleveland
metadata.description: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) has been activated from IR, clearing the way for him to return against Cleveland.
metadata.analysis: Lane has been out since fracturing his wrist in Week 1, so it will be interesting to see what his snap counts and route shares look like after the IR stint. The team praised him all offseason and focused on him during his brief playing time in Week 1, so hopefully he will be able to find himself a decent role as the WR2 of the offense.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Removed from IR
metadata.description: Lane (wrist) was activated from injured reserve by Baltimore on Saturday.
metadata.analysis: Although Lane is still listed as questionable, his activation from IR puts the rookie wide receiver on track to return for Sunday's game against the Browns. Lane was one of the Ravens' standout players during training camp, so he could be featured prominently in the offense alongside Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in his return.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Officially Activated from Injured Reserve for Week 6 Return
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) has been activated from Injured Reserve and will make his return in Week 6 against the Cleveland Browns, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. Lane has been sidelined since fracturing his wrist in Baltimore's Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts. A third-round pick out of USC, Lane hauled in 49 catches for 745 yards and four touchdowns across 11 games in his final collegiate season for the Trojans in 2025. The 22-year-old had one catch for 11 yards on three targets before suffering the wrist injury in his first NFL game. Now that Lane has returned, he could be competing with veteran Ravens wideout Rashod Bateman for the WR2 role in Baltimore behind Zay Flowers.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - On track to be activated from IR
metadata.description: Lane (wrist) is "good to go" after practicing fully this week and is expected to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Lane strung together a trio of full practices to draw the questionable tag for Week 6. It looks like the Ravens will have their rookie third-round wide receiver back on the field for Sunday's AFC North showdown, and Lane could slide right back into the WR2 role behind Zay Flowers and in front of Rashod Bateman. Lane fractured his wrist during the Ravens' Week 1 win against the Colts, when he caught one of three targets for 11 yards (with two of those targets occurring in the end zone).

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane "Good to Go" For Week 6
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is "good to go" after a full practice slate this week, a source told Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. It should facilitate Lane's activation from Injured Reserve for Sunday's Week 6 game against the division-rival Cleveland Browns. The Ravens should officially activate the 22-year-old third-rounder from USC on Saturday, and he should be active on Sunday. Lane caught one of his three targets for 11 yards in his NFL debut in the Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts before injuring his wrist and missing the last four games. Now that he is back in the fold, he will have an opportunity to jump veteran Rashod Bateman as the team's WR2 behind Zay Flowers. Lane was a standout performer for the Ravens during training camp and the preseason this summer, but it remains to be seen if he can get back to that level of performance following his injury. At the very least, Lane is worth a waiver-wire pickup for receiver depth, although we would not recommend using him in starting lineups this weekend with quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) missing a second straight game.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) officially questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
metadata.analysis: The rookie will have a chance to make his return to the field after missing several games while on injured reserve. The team will make a determination about his availability closer to game time, and fantasy managers should temper expectations for him this week, especially with QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) set to be sidelined against Cleveland.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Questionable to return from IR
metadata.description: Lane (wrist) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Cleveland.
metadata.analysis: A full practice participant throughout the week, Lane will need to be taken off injured reserve on Friday or Saturday to play in Sunday's game. If that happens, he'll likely be Baltimore's third or fourth wide receiver, perhaps sharing snaps with Devontez Walker behind veteran starters Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman (both cleared to play after being listed on the injury report this week).

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) practices in full Thursday
metadata.description: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) practiced in a full capacity on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie was able to log a full practice session on Thursday, which was expected. He seems to be primed to make his return to the lineup in the very near future, and we should know what his status is for Week 6 sometime within the next 24 hours or so.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Full participant in practice return
metadata.description: Lane (wrist) was a full participant in practice Wednesday after being designated for return from injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: The Ravens opened Lane's 21-day evaluation window to begin Week 6 prep, after the rookie wideout missed the team's last four games while recovering from left wrist surgery. The rookie wideout was apparently able to stay on top of his conditioning while he was sidelined from practice over the past month, as he faced no limitations in his return to the field. If Lane is able to maintain full practice activity Thursday and Friday, the Ravens could bring him back from IR ahead of Sunday's game in Cleveland.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) practicing in full
metadata.description: Ja'Kobi Lane is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Browns.
metadata.analysis: Lane made his return to practice on Wednesday. He is hopeful to return on Sunday against the Browns.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) expected to practice this week
metadata.description: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is expected to practice this week and has a shot to play this weekend.
metadata.analysis: It's a small sample size, but the Ravens seemed poised to give Lane a sizeable workload before he suffered the injury. He will likely be on some semblance of a snap count to start off, but should be back to full strength soon. He's an intriguing waiver pickup if available.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Could return in Week 6
metadata.description: Lane (wrist) "is expected to return to practice" and per head coach Jesse Minter "has a shot" to play Sunday against the Browns, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Minter said Monday that Lane could be designated to return from injured reserve this week, and it now appears likely he will do so. His participation in practice -- or lack thereof -- from Wednesday through Friday will likely determine whether or not he is ultimately activated for Week 6.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Expected to Practice on Wednesday
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is expected to return to practice on Wednesday. Lane suffered a fractured wrist in Week 1 and was placed on injured reserve. This week marks his first return to practice, and he appears to have a chance to play Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. Although Lane left the opening game early, he appeared to have a significant role early in the 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts. He was the talk of Ravens' training camp, emerging as one of Lamar Jackson's favorite targets, and caught four passes for 47 yards and a touchdown in two preseason appearances. With Zay Flowers cemented as Baltimore's lead receiver, Lane still has a chance to produce fantasy-relevant numbers. He should be rostered in most fantasy leagues, as he's expected to return from injured reserve in Week 6.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Could return to practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that the Ravens could designate Lane (wrist) to return from injured reserve as soon as Wednesday, Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner reports.
metadata.analysis: The rookie third-rounder's offseason momentum was stymied when he fractured his wrist during the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Colts. Minter noted that Lane has kept up his conditioning while on IR, and there's a chance that the 22-year-old wideout could be back on the field for practice as soon as Wednesday, though it's unclear whether he'll be cleared to return for Week 6 against the Browns on Oct. 18.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane has a Chance to Return in Week 6
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday that rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) has put himself in position to have a chance to come off Injured Reserve and return for the team's Week 6 tilt against the division-rival Cleveland Browns on Sunday, according to The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec. This news should make fantasy managers run to the waiver wire to check on the 22-year-old third-rounder's availability. Lane caught just one of three passes for 11 yards in the Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts before fracturing his wrist. He also had a short touchdown reception called back due to a penalty. Lane was the buzz of Baltimore's training camp and preseason as a fast-rising rookie receiver who was quickly gaining chemistry with quarterback Lamar Jackson as a legitimate threat behind WR1 Zay Flowers. Lane's first year in the NFL hit an early roadblock, but he appears to be on the verge of a return and could quickly take over WR2 duties from veteran Rashod Bateman. Lane is only rostered in 8% of Yahoo leagues, so he is widely available to be picked up by fantasy managers searching for WR depth.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Could be Ready to Return in Week 6
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said on Friday that rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is "doing really well" in his rehab from a fractured wrist that landed him on Injured Reserve. Minter added that Lane has put himself in a good spot to be ready to return when he is eligible to come off IR for Week 6. The 22-year-old third-rounder from USC had surgery in mid-September after he injured his wrist in the Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Lane caught only one pass for 11 yards on three targets in his regular-season NFL debut, but he had put himself in position in training camp and the preseason to have a shot to leapfrog veteran Rashod Bateman for the No. 2 role in Baltimore behind Zay Flowers. It remains to be seen if he can jump right back in and demand a big role in the passing attack upon his activation from IR, but fantasy managers should want to find out. Lane is currently rostered in under 10% of Yahoo leagues, and he could be back as early as Oct. 18 against the division-rival Cleveland Browns.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Making good progress with rehab
metadata.description: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Friday that Lane (wrist) is "doing really well" and "has put himself in a great position to be ready to roll when the time permits."
metadata.analysis: Lane is eligible to return from injured reserve for Week 6, and while Minter didn't get into specifics, it does sounds like the rookie wideout is expected back fairly soon. Lane underwent surgery in mid-September after fracturing his wrist in a Week 1 win over the Colts. He played 24 snaps on offense in the first half of that game, catching one of three targets for 11 yards, with a short TD catch called back due to a penalty. Lane could be the team's No. 2 or 3 wide receiver when he returns.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Still a Priority Stash in Deeper Leagues
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) remains sidelined through Week 5 at the earliest, but he still has some appeal as a player to stash in deeper leagues, especially those that offer injured reserve slots. Lane underwent wrist surgery after the season opener, in which he played 40% of the snaps with three targets, one catch, and 11 yards. The rookie USC product was a third-round pick and has big-play upside, but he'll need to get healthy before he even begins to climb up the depth chart. Once he does return, he'll be no higher than third on the depth chart, putting him behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman. With that said, Bateman has an iffy track record of production and Flowers is still less than 100% after a hamstring injury, so Lane could have a path to a meaningful role by the second half of the season. Managers with an open roster spot in deeper leagues should consider stashing Lane in a low-risk move.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Undergoes wrist surgery
metadata.description: Coach Jesse Minter said Lane underwent wrist surgery Wednesday, and the Ravens placed the rookie wide receiver on injured reserve, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
metadata.analysis: Lane left the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis with a wrist injury that eventually was confirmed to include a fracture. With his move to IR, he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Oct. 18 at Cleveland. As long as Lane is sidelined, Zay Flowers (hamstring), Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker (groin), Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester will be among those that could see additional action at wide receiver for Baltimore.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) placed on IR
metadata.description: Ja'Kobi Lane was placed on the injured reserve on Wednesday and will miss the next four games.
metadata.analysis: Lane underwent wrist surgery on Tuesday, and the team is hopeful that he won't miss much more than the required four games for an IL stint. In his absence, Rashod Bateman could be in for more targets, along with Devontez Walker and Elijah Sarratt.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Placed on Injured Reserve
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is being placed on injured reserve after undergoing surgery Wednesday, according to Ian Rapoport. Lane fractured his wrist in Sunday's win over Indianapolis and will now miss at least four games. The rookie had worked his way into Baltimore's No. 3 receiver role before the injury and caught one of three targets for 11 yards in his NFL debut. He also had a touchdown wiped out by a holding penalty. The Ravens are expected to promote Chris Moore from the practice squad to take Lane's roster spot, while Devontez Walker and Elijah Sarratt are also candidates for more work while he is out. Lane is worth keeping in an IR spot in dynasty and deeper leagues, but redraft managers without one do not need to hold him through the absence.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) expected to undergo surgery, miss one month
metadata.description: Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane is expected to undergo surgery in the coming days.
metadata.analysis: Lane could undergo surgery as early as Wednesday. They are hopeful he'll only miss about one month.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Expected to undergo wrist surgery
metadata.description: Lane (wrist) is expected to undergo surgery in the coming days, potentially as soon as Wednesday, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
metadata.analysis: Lane suffered a fractured wrist in the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Colts on Sunday, and now that he's set for surgery, the rookie wideout is hopeful to miss only "about a month," according to Zenitz. With Zay Flowers (hamstring) also less than 100 percent, the Ravens could be dipping into their wideout depth early in the 2026 campaign. Rashod Bateman, Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester picked up the slack against Indy, but Devontez Walker (groin) and rookie Elijah Sarratt could join the mix Sunday against the Saints.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Expected to Have Wrist Surgery
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens promising rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is currently expected to undergo surgery on his fractured wrist in the coming days, potentially as soon as Wednesday, sources told Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. The current hope is that Lane will be able to return in around a month. The 22-year-old third-rounder from USC caught one of his three targets for 11 yards in the Week 1 season-opening win over the Indianapolis Colts before fracturing his wrist, but his fantasy stock had been on the rise going into the season opener as Baltimore's No. 2 wideout behind Zay Flowers (hamstring). With Flowers also injured in Week 1, the Ravens could be looking at a top-three pass-catcher group of veteran Rashod Bateman, rookie Elijah Sarratt, and Devontez Walker (groin) for their Week 2 matchup this Sunday at home against the New Orleans Saints. Lane is a viable receiver to stash in deeper fantasy leagues while his fractured wrist heals. He is currently rostered in 18% of Yahoo leagues.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Receiving further opinions on wrist
metadata.description: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Lane will receive second and third medical opinions on his injured wrist this week before a timeline for his return is established, Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sun reports.
metadata.analysis: Lane's NFL debut in Sunday's 41-23 win over the Colts came to an early end due to the wrist injury, which was confirmed to be a fracture after the game. An upcoming MRI along with additional testing on the wrist should help the Ravens gain a better understanding of the severity of the fracture, but at the very least, the rookie third-round pick is expected to miss the team's Week 2 game against the Saints. Lane's likely absence could open up more opportunities for Devontez Walker (groin) and Eljiah Sarratt (coach's decision), both of whom sat out the season opener.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Getting Second and Third Opinions on Fractured Wrist
metadata.description: The Baltimore Sun's Sam Cohn says that Baltimore Ravens rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) might be out a bit longer since he is getting second and third opinions on his fractured wrist this week. Lane's timetable for a return is unclear right now, but fantasy managers who have him rostered in deeper leagues should be expecting a multi-week absence at the very least. It is unfortunate timing for the 22-year-old from USC, who had opened his first NFL season as Baltimore's WR2 behind Zay Flowers (hamstring) after a strong training camp and preseason. In his NFL debut in the Week 1 season-opening win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, the third-rounder caught just one of his three targets for 11 yards before fracturing his wrist. With Flowers up in the air to play in Week 2 versus the New Orleans Saints, veteran Rashod Bateman and rookie Elijah Sarratt, who was a healthy inactive in Week 1, could be in line for much bigger roles in the Ravens' passing attack. Lane is currently rostered in 18% of Yahoo leagues.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) out for several weeks with broken wrist
metadata.description: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) will miss the next several weeks with a broken wrist he suffered in the Ravens win against the Colts.
metadata.analysis: Lane was seeing some promising usage before exiting with his injury, having a touchdown nullified by holding, another endzone target just out of his reach, and an 11-yard gain on his one reception. The Ravens are now short on receivers unless Zay Flowers, who also exited with an injury, can come back for next week's game. In his absence, expect more work for Rashod Bateman, Chris Moore, and potentially fellow rookie Elijah Sarratt.

metadata.title: Ja'Kobi Lane - Suffers fractured wrist
metadata.description: Lane (wrist) suffered a fractured wrist in Sunday's 41-23 win over the Colts and will undergo further testing Monday, including an MRI, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Lane is expected to face a multi-week absence due to the fractured wrist he sustained in his NFL debut, which led to the rookie third-round pick exiting the game after catching one of three targets for 11 yards. A more precise timetable for Lane's recovery will likely be established after the results of his MRI come in, but he will almost certainly sit out Week 2 against the Saints.
